- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.6) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 3–5 days.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.4) or shows strong bearish momentum, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 2–5% for next 3–5 days.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +10%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots in subsequent days; apply a “cool-down” correction: subtract 3–8% from forecast for next 5–10 days.
- If model forecast is significantly above true outcome (e.g., >10% higher), check sentiment for recent volatility — if sentiment is neutral or mixed, reduce forecast by 5–10% to align with mean reversion.
- If model forecast is significantly below true outcome (e.g., >10% lower), sentiment is often bullish — increase forecast by 5–10% to capture sentiment-driven rebound.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture short-term sentiment shifts; use sentiment from last 5–7 days to adjust final 5–7 days of forecast.
- If sentiment shows strong divergence from price trend (e.g., sentiment bullish but price falling), model tends to lag — adjust forecast upward by 3–7% for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is flat or neutral, model often overfits historical patterns — reduce forecast by 3–5% to avoid overconfidence in past trends.
